title: Swe senior systemdesign distributed job scheduler
topic: Swe senior systemdesign distributed job scheduler
question: Design a distributed job scheduler that runs recurring jobs (like 'send this report every day at 9am') across a fleet of worker machines, where any single machine can go down at any time.
idealAnswer:
Separates scheduling (deciding a job is due) from execution (a worker actually running it), and describes how due jobs get handed off to available workers rather than one component doing both

Addresses the at-most-once requirement directly: uses a claim/lease mechanism (e.g. a worker atomically claims a job with a lease, backed by a database row lock or similar) so two workers can't both pick up and execute the same scheduled run

Handles worker failure mid-execution: a lease with a timeout, so if a worker dies while holding a job, the lease expires and the job becomes claimable again, rather than being stuck forever, and explains why this can occasionally cause a missed or delayed run instead of a duplicate one, matching the stated requirement

Addresses the scheduler itself being a single point of failure, e.g. running multiple scheduler instances with leader election, or making the 'find due jobs' step itself safe to run redundantly since claiming is what actually prevents duplicates

Mentions persisting job state and next-run-time durably (not in-memory only), so a full restart of the scheduling layer doesn't lose track of what's scheduled or when it last ran
